Summary:
This paper describes SystemD, an interactive visual data–analysis tool that lets non-technical business users run “what-if” explorations to discover relationships between data attributes and their key-performance indicators (KPIs). The authors motivate the work by noting that growing data complexity and limited tooling lead to sub-optimal, intuition-driven decisions. They enumerate four core functionalities, implement them in SystemD, and report positive feedback from three real-world business-analysis scenarios.  

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83] – The extracted fabric covers every causal step the paper explicitly presents, links both proposed interventions to the same chain of reasoning, decomposes the “SystemD” framework into white-box nodes, and removes isolated concepts. The JSON passed syntactic and cross-reference checks. The main uncertainties come from sparse methodological details that limit the precision of confidence scores.

Inference-strategy justification:
• Moderate inference (confidence 2) was used to formalise the two interventions (“implement SystemD” and “enhance UX”) because the paper discusses them qualitatively rather than as explicit prescriptions.  
• Otherwise, edges closely follow the stated narrative, with confidence assigned according to the strength of user-study evidence (medium).

Extraction-completeness explanation:
All six concept categories appear at least once and form a single connected fabric from the top-level risk to every intervention. Duplicate or atomic nodes were merged or expanded to maintain mergeable granularity.

Key limitations:
• Only three small case studies support validation; stronger empirical evidence could raise edge confidence.  
• Paper lacks detailed algorithmic specifics, so the “implementation mechanism” node stays high-level.
